Jordan —

Thanks for the call this morning. We ran the numbers after our exec review and want to explore options that balance price certainty with the growth we expect Q4->Q1. A couple constraints from our side:

- We need a mechanism to keep unit pricing within a 10% band for 12 months (finance requirement).
- We expect a 60-80% jump in steady-state consumption after the feature launch in November.
- We can consider a heavier commit if there are credits tied to delivery SLAs.

Can you send a proposal that shows: (1) a consumption-hedge structure that limits upside overage exposure, (2) a scaled-commit covenant that phases in additional committed units, and (3) any short-term credits you can offer for signing by Oct 15?

Appreciate it — Aisha

Thanks Aisha — good call. Attaching a concise proposal (Redwood_Consumption_Hedge_Proposal_v3.pdf) and a usage appendix with last 12 months of token patterns. High level summary below: 

1) Consumption hedge: a two-way collar where effective per-token rate is anchored to current commit +/- 10% (meets finance band request). Above the collar, overage billing uses a softened step (50% of list overage rate for the first 25% spike; then full overage beyond that).

2) Scaled-commit covenant: commit tiers that auto-unlock on verified adoption milestones (metrics from your telemetry). If unlocked, committed pool increases at pre-agreed discounted rates; failure to hit milestones rolls back the next tranche.

3) Signing incentive: a one-time credit equal to 6% of year-one committed spend if contract signed before Oct 15; additional SLA credit (2%) tied to 99.9% inference availability during the ramp window.

Next steps: would love to review this with finance and legal. Suggested internal reviewers: Marissa (pricing authority), Ben (sales ops), Lauren (legal). Aisha — can you confirm the right Novacorp legal contact and whether a PO or DocuSign is preferred?

Proposed short meeting: Wed Sep 29, 11:00am PT — 30 min. If that works I can send a calendar invite and a brief one-page compare vs your current contract.

Thanks,
Jordan

--
